To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a DNA methylation signature derived from BRC1 mutation carriers is associated with sporadic breast cancer and is independent of known breast cancer risk factors.
we found that a DNA methylation signature derived from BRC1 mutation carriers is predictive of sporadic breast cancer risk and mortality.
a blood-based DNA methylation signature derived from BRC1 mutation carriers was able to predict non hereditary breast cancer risk in two independent cohorts and also predict breast cancer mortality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of a novel blood-based DNA methylation signature for the early prediction of sporadic breast cancer.
the development of DNA methylation biomarkers for early breast cancer detection and prevention.
the discovery and development of novel biomarkers for early detection of sporadic breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our study shows that a BRCA1-associated DNA methylation signature derived from BRCAA1 mutation carriers is a promising candidate biomarker for breast cancer risk and mortality prediction.
the blood cell DNA methylation signature derived from women with BRCA1 mutations can predict breast cancer incidence and mortality in the general population.
a DNAme signature derived in blood cells from BRCA1-mutated women can predict sporadic breast cancer risk and survival.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a BRCA1 DNAme signature is able to predict future breast cancer risk, but not in the same way that a BRCA mutation is able to predict risk.
the BRCA1 mutation-associated DNAme signature is predictive of sporadic breast cancer risk and mortality.
the DNAme signature is able to predict sporadic breast cancer and death years in advanced of diagnosis and is independent of other known risk factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
DNAme signatures can be developed from a small cohort of mutation carriers and used to predict non-heritable disease.
a DNAme signature derived in one population is not necessarily generalizable to another population.
DNAme signatures derived from cancer predisposition syndromes are able to identify sporadic cancer cases.
